learning_outcomes.text: Have an increased depth of knowledge and skills in the use of the modern features-based 3D modeller.
Use a modern features-based 3D modeller to create assemblies.

Use materials selection methodologies and relevant software to make rational choices on the basis of engineering, considering manufacturing techniques and other parameters affecting the final costs of products.

syllabus_topics: Development of a functional understanding of 3D modelling practises within the Solidworks platform.
Understand the importance of, and adhere to, international standards for computer aided modelling.
Creation of parts and assemblies within Solidworks.
Understand the classifications and the terminology to describe materials and their properties.
Utilise a design process for materials selection to identify, compare and analyse appropriate materials.
Implement the stages of a materials selection design process in Granta EduPack software.
teaching_methods: Lectorial format (short teaching bursts interspersed with assisted lab-based tutorials)
assessment_rules: Students must gain a summative mark of 40% to pass the module. Students who fail the module at the first attempt will be re-assessed during the July/August exam diet. This re-assessment will consist entirely of examination. No marks from any previous attempts will be transferred to a new resit attempt.
bibliography: Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th Ed, Michael Ashby, Butterworth-Heinemann, ISBN-10: 1856176630, 2010.
